Subject: Re: Pilot SLO hardware slate & acceptance criteria

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap from my side and a few clarification asks so we can move the pilot into procurement.

High-level requirements we discussed (HelioHealth production target):
- Workload: synchronous chat assistant used in clinician workflow (prompt + model -> streaming response).
- Typical response length: 40–120 tokens (median ~70).
- Target SLOs: p50 first-byte < 120ms, p95 first-byte < 300ms for <=64-token responses; streaming token cadence acceptable at ~30–50ms/token for subsequent tokens.
- Concurrency & throughput: sustain 120 active concurrent sessions during peak (expected burst to 180 for <10 min), average sustained throughput ~1,200 requests/min (20 rps) with spikes to 40 rps.
- Availability/ops: need per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown for the pilot.

Questions we still have:
1) For the SLOs above, which GPU slate (A10G vs A100 40GB vs H100) do you recommend for initial pilot vs long-term reserved capacity? We want a cost-efficient pilot but realistic headroom.
2) What reserved-throughput numbers should we commit for the pilot (tokens/sec or concurrent slots)? Helio's procurement needs a conservative baseline to size a short-term commitment.
3) Acceptance criteria for pilot: can you propose 3 gating checks we must pass before we move to Dedicated Reserved? (e.g., p95 latency, sustained throughput for X minutes, failover behavior)

I attached Helio's SLO matrix and a draft procurement intent PDF. Aaron (procurement) included here for scheduling PO/invoice steps.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Director, Platform Integrations
HelioHealth

Subject: Re: Pilot SLO hardware slate & acceptance criteria

Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments, helpful. Below are concrete recommendations and a proposed pilot acceptance checklist so procurement has something tangible.

Recommended pilot hardware slates (two options):
- Cost-focused pilot (fast validation, lower spend): 3 x NVIDIA A10G (32GB) nodes with mixed-precision (Q4/Q8) and Redwood quantization profiles. Expected to meet p50/p95 for typical 70-token replies under optimized batching/caching; good mirror of production cost profile.
- Performance-focused pilot (latency headroom): 1–2 x NVIDIA A100 (40GB) nodes (larger memory + better FP16 kernels). Use for a short 48–72h baseline to measure headroom vs A10G.
- Long-term option we can discuss after pilot: H100 slab for peak-heavy tiers — recommended only if benchmarks show sustained >2x throughput demand vs A100.

Reserved throughput guidance (pilot):
- Commit to a conservative floor: reserve capacity for 40 rps sustained equivalent (this maps to roughly 2–3 A10G equivalents depending on quantization and batching). We will run an internal benchmark mapping tokens/sec for your prompt shapes and return a precise token/sec -> node count table before PO.

Pilot acceptance criteria (proposed gates):
1) Latency gate: p95 first-byte <= 320ms for <=64-token responses during a 30-minute steady-state run at target concurrency (120).
2) Throughput gate: sustain 1,200 req/min for 15 continuous minutes without queue growth >5% and without CPU/GPU throttling errors.
3) Regression & failover gate: failover to a lower-cost model variant (quantized) must not increase p95 beyond 25% and must preserve functional correctness on our eval prompt set.

Operational checkpoints we will enable for the pilot: token-level cost dashboards, per-route SLO traces, and an A/B rollout where we shift 10% traffic to a quantized variant to observe regressions. Karthik will own the benchmark config and provide the harness.

Next steps:
- We’ll produce a short benchmark plan (workload generator + acceptance harness) and attach it to the PO.
- Proposed pilot window: week of Sep 4 (Tue–Thu) — is that acceptable from your side?

Ben — can you put together a quick cost delta estimate (3x A10G vs 1x A100) so procurement has a figure to evaluate?

Happy to jump on a quick sync if needed.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in a few implementation specifics for the benchmark & pilot run so the acceptance checks are measurable. Notes below are for our benchmark harness and the runbook.

Benchmark config & perf knobs:
- Model variants: baseline FP16 (A100), quantized Q4_K_M (A10G) and a mixed-precision fallback. We'll evaluate both throughput and token-emission latency.
- Batching: use adaptive continuous batching with a target latency ceiling of 150ms to keep p50 tight. For p95 we will cap batch size at 8 for chat paths.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching for clinician prompts (common templates). Expect ~25–35% token reduction on cached paths which buys headroom.
- Telemetry: capture token timestamps, GPU utilization, host-side queue latency, and Redwood per-route slot usage.

Measurement plan:
- Run three workload phases: (1) ramp to 120 concurrent sessions steady for 30m; (2) 10-minute spike to 180 concurrent sessions; (3) 30-minute soak at 20 rps for throughput stability.
- Acceptance gating: automate p95/p50 computes and generate an artifacts bundle (benchmark logs + perf traces).

Quick ask for procurement sizing: we will translate the pilot run numbers into a recommended reserved-slab. My initial heuristic: if A10G pilot sustains your p95 with <70% GPU utilization after KV caching, recommend scaling to a 6-node A10G slab for production reserve. If A100 shows >50% headroom at pilot scale, recommend 2 A100 equivalents. We will provide exact token/sec -> node mapping after the pilot.

I will prepare the harness and share the exact test scripts by EOD Mon Aug 3 (typo: Sep 3).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
